# ZecPy

> ZecPy is a Python SDK for sending and receiving shielded Zcash, built on librustzcash through a Rust extension. It is private by default: its light server receives no request that identifies the wallet, sends go over Tor, transparent recipients are refused, and payments are matched to invoices by diversified address, not by memo.

Amounts are integers in zatoshis (1 ZEC = 100,000,000). Every network call is async. `PrivacyError` is a deliberate refusal; do not work around it with `allow_transparent` or `allow_pool_crossing` unless the user asked for exactly that. Each link below is a clean Markdown page; llms-full.txt holds all of them in one file.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](docs/index.md): What ZecPy is, who it is for, and what it looks like in code.
- [Installation](docs/installation.md): Requirements, building from source, and checking the install.
- [Quick start](docs/quickstart.md): Create a wallet, take a payment against an invoice, and send ZEC, step by step.
- [ZecPy Live demo](docs/demo.md): A walkthrough page that runs ZecPy through five scenes on a real chain and shows every request its light server receives.

## Guides

- [Accept payments](docs/accept-payments.md): Invoices with their own shielded addresses, exactly-once payment events, and a checkout API with signed webhooks.
- [Send and batch payouts](docs/send-payments.md): Single payments, up to 50 recipients in one transaction, payroll from a CSV, and broadcast delays.
- [Preview fees and sweep](docs/fees-and-sweeps.md): Plan a payment before building it, send exactly what was shown, and empty a wallet with nothing left behind.
- [Cold signing](docs/cold-signing.md): Run the online server with a viewing key only; sign on an offline machine with zecpy-cold.
- [Agent payments](docs/agent-payments.md): Let a bot or AI agent pay ZIP-321 links within a hard budget it cannot be talked out of.
- [Memos and history](docs/memos-and-history.md): Read transaction history locally, and fetch received memos only when you opt in, among decoys and over Tor.
- [Local devnet](docs/devnet.md): A private regtest chain (zebrad and lightwalletd) for development, tests and the demo.

## Reference

- [API reference](docs/api.md): Every public class, method and field in the zecpy package.
- [Errors](docs/errors.md): The exception hierarchy, what each one means, and how to handle it.
- [Command-line tools](docs/cli.md): zecpy-cold, the offline signer, and the leak-audit proxy.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): Build problems, Tor, testnet funds and devnet quirks.

## AI agents

- [For AI agents](docs/agents.md): Machine-readable docs, a brief to paste into an agent's instructions, and an AGENTS.md for your repo.

## Optional

- [Privacy model](docs/privacy.md): What a light server can learn from a ZecPy wallet, how that is measured, and what is still visible.
- [Testnet run](docs/testnet-run.md): A full merchant run on public testnet, every request the shop sent recorded on its way to the server over Tor.
- [How it works](docs/architecture.md): A Python API over a Rust core over librustzcash, a sync loop of its own, and the leak-audit proxy that measures it.
- [Source code](https://github.com/xerodahdev/zecpy): the SDK, examples, tests and the leak-audit proxy
- [ZecPy Live](https://github.com/xerodahdev/zecpy-demo): the demo page and its recorded run
- [Everything in one file](llms-full.txt)
